newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 29.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In an address to the Australia-China Business Council in Sydney, Chinese vice-premier for economic affairs and a contender for the position of Premier, Zhu Rongji, said that in order to enjoy improved relations with China, the Australian Government must keep a formal distance from Taiwan. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard has assured the Pharmacy Guild of Australia that the industry will not be subject to competition reforms until at least 1999. Howard's assurance follows a pre-election promise, and will assist pharmacists in their battle to retain a monopoly over the supply of prescription drugs. Page 3.

The failure of the Federal Government to appoint a new Sex Discrimination Commissioner after the resignation of Sue Walpole could see the investigation of sexual harassment and discrimination grind to a halt from midnight tonight. Walpole had delegated her powers to another Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission officer for a period of three months to give time to find a replacement, yet that three month period ends at midnight tonight. Page 3.

Prime Minister John Howard demanded and received a retraction and apology from West Australian Liberal Ross Lightfoot, after Lightfoot said in the Senate that Aborigines were the "lowest colour on the civilisation spectrum". Howard warned Lightfoot he wold be ejected from the Liberal Party room if he failed to apologise for his comments. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The prospect of a double dissolution election over Prime Minister John Howard's 10-point Wik plan was raised yesterday as the Federal Government's Aboriginal policy became the focus of an emotional day of Parliament. Howard threatened to expel newly apponted WA Senator Ross Lightfoot for racist comments, as Opposition Leader Kim Beazley broke down when responding to the stolen generation report. Page 1.

Under proposed media ownership changes indicated by Communications Minister Richard Alston, foreign ownership limits would be increased, allowing Rupert Murdoch's News Ltd to buy 25 percent of the Seven Network, and Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasing Ltd to takeover the Fairfax newspaper group. Page 1.

Chinese Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji indicated yesterday he was concerned about Australia's relationship with Taiwan, yet told a Sydney lunch the Australian Government had assured him of its commitment to the one-China policy. Zhu said China would not interfere with Australia's trade relations with Taipei so long as these were conducted through unofficial contacts. Page 1.

In an effort to increase its funds, the Sydney University is set to demolish lecture theatres to make way for a A$40 million, 188-bed private teaching hospital on campus that would be run by Health Care of Australia, a division of Mayne Nickless. The plan has been criticised by both staff and students. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New South Wales Labor MP Paul Lynch, Member for Liverpool, has been accused by some of his former supporters within the party of offering them inducements to join the Australian Labor Party and help secure his preselection against former minister Peter Anderson. Page 1.

Frank Gilford reiterated yesterday that if found guilty of his sister Yvonne's murder, two British nurses, Deborah Parry and Lucille McLaughlan, must die. The women are being held in a jail in Saudi Arabia, the country where the murder took place, and under Islamic law if the two are to die, they will be publicly beheaded. Page 1.

Communications Minister Richard Alston outlined a six-point plan to the Coalition's backbench communications committee on Tuesday night, in an attempt to find a compromise to settle backbench concerns over media diversity. The plan will scrap the cross-media rules in Sydney and Melbourne and clear the way for the expansion plans of Kerry Packer and Rupert Murdoch. Page 1.

Following a phone call from Prime Minister John Howard over his comments at the Reconciliation Convention in Melbourne this week, Governor-General Sir William Deane issued a statement saying he regretted that his comments on the Constitution's race power had become a political issue. Page 1.
THE AGE

A senior United States-based executive of Intergraph says the company paid US$4 million to heads of Intergraph Australia Grant Griffiths and Shane Tyrrell, the men who managed Intergraph's controversial emergency dispatch system in Melbourne, to end their association with the company. Page 1.

Under a plan being considered by the Federal Government, Kerry Packer would be able to take over the Fairfax media company on the condition he sold either The Age or The Sydney Morning Herald. The plan would also see American citizen Rupert Murdoch retain his dominant stake in Australia's newspaper industry, while also increasing his stake in the Seven Network to 25 percent. Page 1.

Brigitte Muir, of Nathmuk in western Victoria, yesterday became the first Australian woman to climb Mount Everest. Her husband Jon said yesterday his wife was successful on what was her fourth attempt, yet she still faced the problem of getting off the mountain. Page 1.

Frank Gilford, whose sister Yvonne was murdered in Saudi Arabia, said yesterday the death penalty for Englishwomen Deborah Parry and Lucille McLachlan, who are accused with the murder, seemed to be the only right answer in the situation. A Saudi Arabian court trial has been adjourned so lawyers can consult the Gilford family to negotiate a reconsideration to spare the nurses. Page A1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
